question.problem:
Let $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ be a linear transformation with standard matrix $T$ whose columns are ${v}_{1},$
 ${v}_{2},$ and  ${v}_{3}.$

*If  $\text{dim}(\text{Span}\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\})=1$, then $\text{__________}.$ *

Which of the following, if inserted into the blank space, would lead to a true statement?

I. $\text{nullity}(T)=2$

II. ${x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}+{x}_{3}{v}_{3}=0$ has only the trivial solution

III. $\text{rank}(T)=2$
question.worked_solution:
Since $T$ is a linear transformation from ${R}^{3}$ into ${R}^{3},$ the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

 $T$ is a bijection (an invertible transformation) $\,⟺\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Im}(T)={R}^{3} \\  & \text{rank}(T)=3 \\  & \text{Ker}(T)=\{0\} \\  & \text{nullity}(T)=0\end{aligned}$ 

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, 

$$
\text{rank}(T)+\text{nullity}(T)=3.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Since $\text{dim}(\text{span}\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\})=1$ this means that $\text{rank}(T)=1.$ According to the rank-nullity theorem, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{nullity}(T) & =3-\text{rank}(T) \\  & =3-1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, according to the invertible matrix theorem the linear transformation $T$ cannot be a bijection.

- Statement II is false. Notice that ${x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}+{x}_{3}{v}_{3}=0$ is equivalent to $Tx=0.$ Since $T$ is not invertible, the equation has non-trivial solutions.

- Statement III is false. From statement I, $\text{rank}(T)=1.$

Therefore, the correct option is "I only."

choices.value: None of the statements are true
